Laura / team,

Initial findings from the runtime team: around 07:45 PT a kernel selection change that was rolled to the hosted fleet for model-gen-1.1 triggered a fallback path for certain sequence lengths that causes excessive tokenization and KV cache churn on long-prefix requests. The symptom matches the traces BrightShore sent — many requests are hitting >1024 token prefixes.

What we did so far:
- Immediately rolled back the kernel selector change to previous stable at 08:00 PT for the affected host pool.
- Redeployed a hotfix to prevent repeated re-evaluation for active KV cache entries at 08:20 PT.
- Temporarily increased prefix cache TTL to reduce cache churn.

Current state: P95 is down to 350–500ms on the majority of hosts; P99 is still elevated at ~1.1–1.8s for requests hitting the long-prefix path. Error rate (5xx) dropped to ~0.6%. We're continuing to sweep the host pool for stragglers.

Next steps:
1) Continue host pool sweep and patch rollout (ETA 90 minutes).
2) Add traffic reroute for BrightShore to insulated capacity if needed (can be done in ~30 min).
3) Prepare a customer-facing incident note for status.redwood.ai (Marissa — can you push one ASAP?).

I'll post an update when the sweep is complete.

— Dev
Dev Patel
